findings.reasoning: search_users interpolates name directly into SQL at line 10 and executes it at line 11. Input `' OR 1=1 --` closes the LIKE literal and replaces the name filter with an always-true condition, returning every user's id, name, and email. Ordinary names containing apostrophes can also cause SQL syntax errors.
findings.title: Search input allows SQL injection
findings.body: Bind the LIKE pattern as a parameter, following get_user: conn.execute("SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE name LIKE ?", (f"%{name}%",)).

failure_scenario.input: Call search_users(conn, "' OR 1=1 --") with a populated users table.
failure_scenario.expected: Treat the input as search text and return only matching users.
failure_scenario.actual: The injected OR condition matches every row, returning all users and their email addresses.
